flaws.title: Downward iterator skips the initialized start tick, so active liquidity is wrong when the swap starts exactly on an initialized tick
flaws.sequence:
1. The pool has tickSpacing 10, an existing position over [0,30) and the current tick is exactly 30. Tick 30 is initialized as the upper bound of the position, and Uniswap's active liquidity at 30 leaves out [0,30). If the tick is not already 30, the attacker first swaps one-for-zero to reach it.
2. The attacker adds liquidity L' to [20,30) and pays the JIT tax.
3. The attacker makes the top-of-block zero-for-one swap down to just below 30. afterSwap calls _zeroForOneDistributeTax, which calls initDown(start=30, end=29), and that calls reset(30).
4. reset sets currentTick to 30 and calls _advanceToNextDown. That function looks at compress(30-1), which is the bit for tick 20, so tick 30 is never returned. The later ticks.reset(slot0BeforeSwap.tick()) call skips 30 again.
5. In CompensationPriceFinder.getZeroForOne and _zeroForOneCreditRewards, liquidity starts at liquidityBeforeSwap and never has liquidityNet(30) subtracted. The new L' is therefore never counted.
6. The leftover tax is turned into growth per unit of liquidity using this too-small liquidity value, so globalGrowthX128 rises far more than it should. The attacker's [20,30) position earns growth g on L' and can claim about all reward balance R.
7. In another setup with no overlapping liquidity, the later liquidity.sub(liquidityNet) at the lower tick underflows and the top-of-block swap reverts.
flaws.impact: An attacker can steal the accumulated LP rewards. In other tick layouts, top-of-block zero-for-one swaps revert, and tax is given to the wrong LPs.
flaws.known_finding: All rewards can be stolen due to incorrect active liquidity calculations when the current tick is an exact multiple of the tick spacing at the upper end of a liquidity range

requirement_breaks: Requirement 4/5 is not met when startTick is an initialized multiple of the tick spacing. That tick's liquidityNet is needed to go from active liquidity at startTick to active liquidity at endTick, but reset never returns it.
